punchline: The stuttering lawyer Dave Walton told the jury openly that he stuttered, and the jury listened to him more.
thirty_sec: The Dave Walton that Adam Grant describes was a lawyer who stuttered. Instead of hiding his weakness, he told the jury openly and spoke calmly and sincerely. The jury listened to him more and trusted him more. Grant calls this powerless communication: admitting a flaw, asking for advice, saying "I don't know".
